propositions: Pandoc 3.6.1 corrupts code-span arrows, deletes HTML comments, and erodes tables when converting Markdown to Jira, requiring a segmenting renderer that locks protected blocks and classifies units safely before pandoc conversion.
A two-phase lexer must lock {noformat} spans, HTML comments, backtick/tilde fences, and four-space indented blocks before classification to prevent corruption during conversion.
A post-render code-preservation check must verify every code fragment from source appears verbatim in output, falling back to original Markdown if any fragment is lost or corrupted.

The renderer must split Jira wiki markers into unambiguous forms ({{monospace}}, [label|target], {color:name}) that settle a unit alone and ambiguous forms (*strong*, _emphasis_) that only settle units with no CommonMark-only markers, preventing two-cycle re-rendering.

A corpus of 178 deterministically-generated scrubbed Markdown bodies (29 code-arrow, 29 table, 120 prose) must reach ≥0.90 body ratio and ≥0.95 character ratio of eligible units rendering non-identically, with measured baseline 0.916/0.969.

The implementation must remain unwired (WikiTextCodec and live sends unchanged), handle missing pandoc gracefully with identity fallback, log only fixed-token reasons (pandoc_absent, conversion_failure, preservation_failure), and never log body content.
